# Overview

**Module 2: Alignment**

This module handles:

1. Splitting each reference at its N block into a left and a right flank
2. Aligning every read to each flank with minimap2 (`r params$minimap2_args`)
3. Keeping, per read, the best alignment to each flank (highest MAPQ, then longest)
4. Requiring both flanks, on the same strand, with the left flank before the right
5. Reverse-complementing reads that aligned to the reverse strand, so every read reads 5' to 3' along the reference
6. Optional manual read exclusions

**Outputs:**

- `02_alignment/alignment.xlsx` – read accounting per sample, flank alignment quality
- `02_alignment/plots/` – the figures in this report (per-sample alignment plots in `alignment_by_sample/`)
- `module_data/02_alignment.RData` – strand-corrected reads with flank coordinates, for Module 3

---

# References

Each distinct reference in the tracts table is aligned to separately. Tracts that share a reference are found in the same between-flanks region in Module 3.

```{r references}
m1 <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "01_import_qc.RData")
safe_load_module(m1, 1)
sequences <- module1_output$sequences
samples <- setNames(names(sequences), names(sequences))
tracts <- params$tracts_table
refs <- lapply(unique(tracts$path_ref), parse_reference_sequence)
names(refs) <- vapply(refs, `[[`, "", "ref_id")
if (any(duplicated(names(refs)))) stop("Two references share the FASTA header name: ", paste(names(refs)[duplicated(names(refs))], collapse = ", "))
ref_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(refs, `[[`, "summary")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(tibble(ref_id = names(refs), tracts = vapply(refs, function(r) paste(tracts$tract[tracts$path_ref == r$path], collapse = ", "), "")), by = "ref_id")
dt_compact(ref_table, caption = "Reference flanks (first and last 20 bases of each)")
```

---

# Alignment

```{r align}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
exclusions <- load_manual_read_exclusions(params$path_manual_exclusions)
bam_dir <- file.path(aln_dir, "bam")
results <- lapply(refs, function(ref) {
  apply_fn(samples, function(s) process_sample_alignment(s, sequences[[s]], ref, temp_dir, params$minimap2_args,
                                                         params$keep_bam, bam_dir, exclusions))
})
alignments <- lapply(results, function(r) rbindlist(lapply(r, `[[`, "table")))
funnel <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(results, function(r) dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(r, `[[`, "funnel"))))
rm(results); if (params$remove_intermediate) { rm(sequences); invisible(gc()) }
timings["Alignment and filtering"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
cat(sprintf("%s of %s reads (%.1f%%) span both flanks in the correct order.",
            comma(sum(funnel$final)), comma(sum(funnel$input)), 100 * sum(funnel$final) / max(1, sum(funnel$input))))
```

## Read accounting

Each line is one sample, and the box at each step summarises all samples: the percentage of the sample's input reads still present after that step. A drop at **both flanks** means reads that do not span the locus (primer dimers, truncated products, off-target reads); a drop at **same strand** or **correct order** means chimeric or rearranged reads.

```{r funnel_plot, fig.height=5.5}
steps <- c(input = "Input", aligned_left = "Left flank", aligned_right = "Right flank", both_flanks = "Both flanks",
           same_strand = "Same strand", correct_order = "Correct order", final = "Final")
fl <- funnel %>% dplyr::mutate(n_input = input) %>% pivot_longer(all_of(names(steps)), names_to = "step", values_to = "reads") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(step = factor(steps[step], levels = steps), pct = reads / pmax(n_input, 1))
p_funnel <- ggplot(fl, aes(step, pct)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = interaction(file_stem, ref_id)), colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, colour = "grey30", width = 0.5) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 4, colour = "red") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "text", colour = "red", size = 3.2, vjust = -1.2, aes(label = percent(after_stat(y), 0.1))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1.05)) +
  facet_wrap(~ ref_id) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads remaining (% of input)", title = "Reads remaining after each alignment step",
       subtitle = "Grey lines = samples; red = cohort mean") + theme_bw()
print(p_funnel); save_plot(p_funnel, file.path(plots_dir, "read_accounting.png"), 11, 5.5)
```

```{r funnel_table}
dt_full(funnel, caption = "Reads per sample after each alignment step")
```

## Where the flank alignments end

The repeat-adjacent end of each flank should align to its last (left) or first (right) reference base. Each point is one sample: the percentage of its reads whose flank alignment stops at least one base short of the N block. Reads with a shortfall are not lost – Module 3 searches `r params$rpt_flank_pad` bases into each flank so the tract is still measured in full – but a sample with a high rate has sequence next to the repeat that differs from the reference, for example an interruption variant.

```{r shortfall, fig.height=5}
sf <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(alignments), function(r) {
  a <- alignments[[r]]
  if (!nrow(a)) return(NULL)
  a[, .(`Left flank` = mean(left_end_shortfall > 0), `Right flank` = mean(right_start_shortfall > 0),
        median_left_shortfall = as.numeric(median(left_end_shortfall)), median_right_shortfall = as.numeric(median(right_start_shortfall))), by = file_stem][, ref_id := r]
}))
p_sf <- sf %>% pivot_longer(c(`Left flank`, `Right flank`), names_to = "flank", values_to = "pct") %>%
  ggplot(aes(flank, pct)) + box_points_mean(digits = 3) + facet_wrap(~ ref_id) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads whose flank alignment stops short of the N block", title = "Flank alignment boundaries, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_sf); save_plot(p_sf, file.path(plots_dir, "flank_boundary_shortfall.png"), 8, 5)
```

## Alignment quality and strand

Per-sample mean mapping quality for each flank, and the proportion of reads that aligned to the reverse strand and were reverse-complemented (`+c`). Amplicons sequenced from both ends give about half on each strand.

```{r quality_plot, fig.height=5}
qual <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(alignments), function(r) {
  a <- alignments[[r]]; if (!nrow(a)) return(NULL)
  a[, .(left_mapq = mean(left_mapq), right_mapq = mean(right_mapq), left_mismatch = mean(left_nm, na.rm = TRUE),
        right_mismatch = mean(right_nm, na.rm = TRUE), reverse_strand = mean(strand == "+c"), reads = .N), by = file_stem][, ref_id := r]
}))
p_q1 <- qual %>% pivot_longer(c(left_mapq, right_mapq), names_to = "flank", values_to = "mapq") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(flank = ifelse(flank == "left_mapq", "Left flank", "Right flank")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(flank, mapq)) + box_points_mean() + facet_wrap(~ ref_id) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean MAPQ", title = "Mapping quality per sample") + theme_bw()
p_q2 <- ggplot(qual, aes(ref_id, reverse_strand)) + box_points_mean(digits = 3) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads on the reverse strand", title = "Strand per sample") + theme_bw()
p_quality <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_q1, p_q2, widths = c(2, 1))
print(p_quality); save_plot(p_quality, file.path(plots_dir, "alignment_quality_strand.png"), 11, 5)
```

```{r quality_table}
dt_full(dplyr::left_join(qual, sf, by = c("file_stem", "ref_id")), caption = "Alignment quality per sample", digits = 3)
```

```{r per_sample_alignment, eval=params$visualise_alignment && params$plot_per_sample}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
by_sample_dir <- file.path(plots_dir, "alignment_by_sample")
for (r in names(alignments)) {
  a <- alignments[[r]]
  for (s in unique(a$file_stem)) {
    d <- a[file_stem == s]
    if (nrow(d) > params$visualise_alignment_downsample) { set.seed(123); d <- d[sample(.N, params$visualise_alignment_downsample)] }
    seg <- rbind(d[, .(read = qname, flank = "Left flank", start = left_rstart, end = left_rend, strand)],
                 d[, .(read = qname, flank = "Right flank", start = right_rstart, end = right_rend, strand)])
    seg[, read := factor(read, levels = d$qname[order(d$left_rstart, d$right_rend)])]
    p <- ggplot(seg, aes(x = start, xend = end, y = read, yend = read, colour = strand)) + geom_segment(linewidth = 0.4) +
      facet_wrap(~ flank, scales = "free_x") + scale_colour_manual(values = c(`+` = "#377eb8", `+c` = "#4daf4a")) +
      labs(x = "Reference position (bp)", y = "Reads", title = paste("Flank alignments:", s),
           subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s reads; +c = reverse-complemented", comma(nrow(d)), comma(sum(a$file_stem == s)))) +
      theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
    save_plot(p, file.path(by_sample_dir, paste0(s, "-", safe_path(r), "-alignment.png")), 10, 6)
  }
}
timings["Per-sample plots"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
cat("Per-sample alignment plots written to", by_sample_dir)
```

# Save output

```{r save}
write_excel_function(list(references = ref_table, read_accounting = funnel, alignment_quality = dplyr::left_join(qual, sf, by = c("file_stem", "ref_id"))), xlsx_path)
module2_output <- list(alignments = alignments, refs = refs, funnel = funnel, quality = qual, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "02_alignment.RData")
save(module2_output, file = output_path)
```

**`r comma(sum(funnel$final))`** reads passed to Module 3.
